(a) 
This section and section 3 of this Act shall become effective on the date of enactment of this Act.
 
    (b) 
Subject to subsection (c) of this section, the first section and section 2 of this Act shall become effective on the one hundred and twentieth day following the date of enactment of this Act.
 
    (c) 
For the purposes of the application of sect ion 3304a (b) of title 5, United States Code, as enacted by this Act, in the case of an individual who, prior to the effective date prescribed by subsection (b) of this section, shall have completed the 3-year period referred to in such section 3304a (b), such individual shall be deemed to have completed such 3-year period on such effective date.

fable.w: This section only sets effective dates and a transition rule for when an individual is deemed to have completed a 3-year period under 5 U.S.C. 3304a(b). There is no tempting reading here: it provides for no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: This section and section 3 of this Act shall become effective on the date of enactment of this Act.

qwen_block.w: This section solely defines the effective dates of the statute and related provisions. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or comment periods mentioned.
qwen_block.s: This section and section 3 of this Act shall become effective on the date of enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This is an effective-date provision. It only sets when the Act's sections take effect and how the 3-year period under section 3304a(b) is counted during the transition. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The reference to an individual completing a service period is a timing rule, not participation in a federal decision.
opus.s: This section and section 3 of this Act shall become effective on the date of enactment of this Act.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** This section only sets effective dates, plus a transition rule saying when an individual counts as having completed the 3-year period under 5 U.S.C. 3304a(b). The one tempting reading is that the mention of "an individual" and the federal hiring rules in 3304a involve someone outside the government. They don't: the clause just says when a period counts as completed. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue or object over a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely defines the effective dates of the Act and clarifies how a specific service period is calculated for individuals under federal law. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory input from parties outside the federal government. The mention of an 'individual' is in the context of a legal fiction regarding the completion of a time period, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "individual" mentioned in subsection (c) is an outside party whose status is being determined, implying some form of interaction. However, this is merely a statutory definition of when a time period is deemed completed for legal purposes; it does not involve any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory role for that individual or any other outside entity. The section is purely procedural regarding the effective dates of the Act and the calculation of service periods for federal employees.
